title: Quoting Ted Sanders
summary_raw: In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There's no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that's best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size. In general, models that are bigger will (a) be more performant / reliable, (b) cost more per token, and (c) have better recall of esoteric facts. title: Wall Street for the Physical Buildout
summary_raw: Software is cheap to start. Robots, GPU clusters, and data centers are not. The physical AI buildout will need new ways to finance steel and silicon: lenders, leasing companies, securitization, and hedging products designed around machines and compute. Every great infrastructure boom created financial giants alongside it. Apply for the Winter 2027 batch at ycombinator.com/apply.

title: Own Your Intelligence
summary_raw: Most companies building with AI still rent their intelligence from frontier labs. As open models improve, more companies will want models they can run, train, and control themselves. The opportunity is to turn a company’s workflows, expertise, and failures into specialized models that improve with the business. Apply for the Winter 2027 batch at ycombinator.com/apply.

title: Plaid for Government Benefits
summary_raw: Applying for government benefits means proving the same facts again and again across systems that don’t talk to each other. That creates friction for honest applicants and openings for fraud. Government needs a Plaid-like layer for verified income, tax, and residency data: verify once, apply everywhere. As AI agents begin handling enrollment, trusted data infrastructure becomes even more important. Apply for the Winter 2027 batch at ycombinator.com/apply.
